deals.travelWindow: Oct 20 – 24, cheapest confirmed nonstop; Allegiant flies the route 5 days a week
deals.whyRanked: The cheapest verified fare of the five by a wide margin at $110–165 RT nonstop, and it's the closest major airport to the Great Smoky Mountains — under an hour to the Sugarlands entrance.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown Knoxville's Market Square is small but walkable and easy to explore alone; you'll want a car for the Smokies day, but the park's trailheads are well-marked and solo-safe.

highlights: Market Square for coffee, lunch, and street musicians
World's Fair Park and the Sunsphere
Laurel-Snow or Alum Cave Trail day hike in the Smokies
Cades Cove loop road for wildlife (deer, sometimes black bear)
Ijams Nature Center on the edge of downtown
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, walk Market Square and World's Fair Park, dinner on Gay Street.
Day 2 — Rent a car, drive to Great Smoky Mountains NP, hike Alum Cave Trail (up to Alum Cave Bluffs, ~4.6 mi round trip) or the shorter Laurel Falls Trail if you want easier miles.
Day 3 — Cades Cove scenic loop at dawn for wildlife, or Ijams Nature Center if you'd rather stay closer to town, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown is walkable on its own, but a rental car is close to essential for the Smokies — pick it up at the airport and return it before your flight out.
guide.stayArea: Downtown/Market Square — walkable, close to restaurants, and about 40 minutes from the park entrance.

deals.whyRanked: $176–210 RT nonstop, and the J.N. "Ding" Darling National Wildlife Refuge on Sanibel Island is a 35-minute drive.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown Fort Myers' River District is small and walkable for an evening, but Sanibel and the beaches are spread out and mostly need a car.

highlights: Ding Darling NWR's Wildlife Drive (bike or drive, alligators and roseate spoonbills)
Sanibel Lighthouse Beach for shelling
Downtown River District's riverfront and galleries
Edison and Ford Winter Estates
Captiva sunset at the Mucky Duck
itinerary: Day 1 — Downtown River District walk, dinner along First Street.
Day 2 — Drive to Sanibel, bike the Ding Darling Wildlife Drive in the morning, Lighthouse Beach for shelling in the afternoon.
Day 3 — Edison and Ford Winter Estates, or push out to Captiva for sunset, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: A rental car is essential — Sanibel, Captiva, and the beaches are 20–40 minutes from downtown with no real transit between them.
guide.stayArea: Downtown River District for restaurants and nightlife, or a Fort Myers Beach/Sanibel base if you'd rather wake up near the water.

deals.travelWindow: Sep 15 – 19, cheapest one-stop; nonstop JetBlue/Delta run higher
deals.whyRanked: $184 RT is the floor for the week (one-stop via Atlanta); no national park nearby, but Wekiwa Springs State Park is a quiet 30-minute escape from the theme-park sprawl.
deals.soloWhy: Winter Park and Lake Eola are walkable pockets, but the metro is car-dependent and most attractions are built for groups rather than solo pacing.

highlights: Winter Park's Park Avenue and the Scenic Boat Tour
Lake Eola Park at sunset
Wekiwa Springs State Park's spring-fed swimming hole and trails
Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex (day trip)
Mills 50 district for murals and local food
itinerary: Day 1 — Winter Park: Park Avenue shops, the Scenic Boat Tour on the chain of lakes, dinner nearby.
Day 2 — Wekiwa Springs State Park in the morning (swim, easy trails), Mills 50 for dinner.
Day 3 — Day trip to Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex (~1 h drive), sunset walk around Lake Eola, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Rental car is essential — Orlando has no real transit network and everything is spread across highway exits.
guide.stayArea: Winter Park or the Lake Eola/Downtown Orlando area — walkable and removed from the International Drive tourist strip.

deals.travelWindow: Oct 3 – Nov 7; cheapest nonstop is Southwest at $231 (Oct 3–5), connecting Frontier fares from $212
deals.whyRanked: $212–231 RT for a walkable downtown with live music every night, and Mammoth Cave National Park is a 2-hour drive if you want a park day.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown and The Gulch are dense and walkable, the honky-tonks are built for striking up conversation at the bar solo, and there's an easy day-trip menu if you want a break from the city.

highlights: Broadway honky-tonk crawl (free live music, no cover)
Ryman Auditorium daytime tour
The Parthenon at Centennial Park
Mammoth Cave NP guided cave tour (book ahead)
East Nashville's coffee shops and vintage stores
itinerary: Day 1 — Broadway honky-tonk crawl, Ryman Auditorium, dinner in The Gulch.
Day 2 — Drive north to Mammoth Cave NP (~2 h) for a ranger-led cave tour, or stay local and walk Centennial Park and the Parthenon.
Day 3 — East Nashville coffee and vintage shopping, Country Music Hall of Fame, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown, The Gulch, and East Nashville are walkable or a short rideshare apart. Rent a car only if doing the Mammoth Cave day trip.
guide.stayArea: The Gulch (walkable, quieter at night) or East Nashville (more local, better coffee/food scene).

deals.whyRanked: $217–240 RT nonstop, and Niagara Falls State Park — the oldest state park in the country — is a 20-minute drive.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown Buffalo and Elmwood Village are compact and walkable, and Niagara Falls has tour buses and shuttles from the city if you'd rather skip renting a car.

highlights: Niagara Falls State Park — Terrapin Point and the Cave of the Winds
Elmwood Village for coffee, shops, and galleries
Darwin D. Martin House (Frank Lloyd Wright)
Buffalo AKG Art Museum
Original Anchor Bar for the birthplace of Buffalo wings
itinerary: Day 1 — Elmwood Village walk, Buffalo AKG Art Museum, dinner at the Anchor Bar.
Day 2 — Day trip to Niagara Falls State Park — Terrapin Point, Cave of the Winds, and the Maid of the Mist boat if it's running.
Day 3 — Darwin D. Martin House tour and a walk along the Buffalo waterfront, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown and Elmwood Village are walkable; Niagara Falls is reachable by the NFTA Metro Rail plus a short bus, or an easy 20-minute drive.
guide.stayArea: Elmwood Village — walkable, close to restaurants, and a straightforward drive or bus ride to Niagara Falls.
